description: Foundations: extend the WhatsAppNumber schema with Meta-onboarding fields (apply to live Turso via db:push), add the AES-256-GCM crypto utility + standalone test harness, and add the shared whatsapp helper (normalizePhone, serializeNumber, resolveSendCredentials, NumberOwnedByOtherTenantError, upsertNumberForUser). This is the dependency base for all later features. Independent of FEAT-002/003/004, which build on top of it.
steps: Edit prisma/schema.prisma: add these nullable/defaulted fields to the WhatsAppNumber model, keeping all existing fields including verificationCode: `accessToken String?` (AES-256-GCM ciphertext at rest; inline comment: never plaintext, never logged), `tokenExpiresAt DateTime?`, `displayPhoneNumber String?`, `verifiedName String?`, `qualityRating String?`, `codeVerificationStatus String?`, `platformType String?`, `connectionType String @default("manual")`.
Apply the schema to the live Turso DB with `npm run db:push` (additive nullable columns only — never drop a column).

Create src/lib/crypto.ts exporting `encrypt(plaintext: string): string` returning `base64(iv).base64(tag).base64(ciphertext)` and `decrypt(payload: string): string`. Use `import crypto from "crypto"` (same pattern as src/app/api/payments/verify/route.ts). A lazy private getKey() reads process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY, base64-decodes it, asserts exactly 32 bytes, else throws Error("ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing or not a 32-byte base64 key"). encrypt uses a fresh 12-byte crypto.randomBytes IV with aes-256-gcm. decrypt splits on "."; if not exactly 3 segments throw Error("Invalid ciphertext format"); set the auth tag so decipher.final() throws on tamper. The module must NEVER log.

Create scripts/test-crypto.mjs: a plain .mjs that re-implements the same AES-256-GCM iv.tag.ciphertext base64 format inline using only Node built-in crypto (NO import from src/lib/crypto.ts, no compile, no new dependency). Assert: (1) decrypt(encrypt(x)) === x for a known string; (2) tampering one char of the ciphertext/tag makes decrypt throw; (3) an absent/short ENCRYPTION_KEY throws a clear error. Print a pass line per assertion and exit non-zero on any failure.

Create src/lib/whatsapp.ts. Import `prisma` (default) from "@/lib/db", `decrypt` from "@/lib/crypto", and `Prisma` from "@prisma/client". Export: `normalizePhone(s: string)` => s.replace(/\D/g, ""); `serializeNumber(number)` => a shallow copy of the row with the accessToken property removed; `resolveSendCredentials(number: { phoneNumberId: string | null; accessToken: string | null })` => if number.accessToken is non-null return { phoneNumberId: number.phoneNumberId, accessToken: decrypt(number.accessToken) } (may throw), else return { phoneNumberId: number.phoneNumberId ?? process.env.META_PHONE_NUMBER_ID ?? null, accessToken: process.env.META_ACCESS_TOKEN ?? null }; a `NumberOwnedByOtherTenantError` class extending Error; `upsertNumberForUser({ userId, phoneNumber, data })` implementing find-then-branch: findUnique on phoneNumber -> if existing && existing.userId !== userId throw NumberOwnedByOtherTenantError -> if existing update by existing.id -> else create (userId, phoneNumber, ...data) in a try/catch where a Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError with code 'P2002' rethrows NumberOwnedByOtherTenantError. Do NOT use prisma.whatsAppNumber.upsert.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run db:push` applies the new nullable WhatsAppNumber columns against the live Turso DB with no data loss (AC #2).
`npm run build` (prisma generate && next build) completes with no type or build errors, with the new src/lib/crypto.ts and src/lib/whatsapp.ts type-checking (AC #1).
`ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(openssl rand -base64 32) node scripts/test-crypto.mjs` passes all three assertions and exits 0 (AC #9).
src/lib/whatsapp.ts uses find-then-branch (no prisma upsert) and resolveSendCredentials prefers the row's decrypted token, falling back to env only when accessToken is null (supports AC #10).
findings:
COMPLETED. Exported symbols for later features:

src/lib/crypto.ts:
- `encrypt(plaintext: string): string` -> returns `base64(iv).base64(tag).base64(ciphertext)` (dot-separated, aes-256-gcm, 12-byte IV). Never logs.
- `decrypt(payload: string): string` -> reverses encrypt; throws Error('Invalid ciphertext format') if not exactly 3 dot segments; throws on tamper via decipher.final(). Never logs.
- Lazy getKey() reads process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY (base64, must decode to exactly 32 bytes) else throws Error('ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing or not a 32-byte base64 key'). Key resolved at call time, not import time.

src/lib/whatsapp.ts (imports: `import { Prisma } from "@prisma/client"`, `import prisma from "@/lib/db"`, `import { decrypt } from "@/lib/crypto"`):
- `normalizePhone(s: string): string` => s.replace(/\D/g, "").
- `serializeNumber<T extends { accessToken?: string | null }>(number: T): Omit<T, "accessToken">` => shallow copy with accessToken removed. Use before returning any WhatsAppNumber row in an API response.
- `resolveSendCredentials(number: { phoneNumberId: string | null; accessToken: string | null }): { phoneNumberId: string | null; accessToken: string | null }` => if accessToken !== null returns { phoneNumberId: number.phoneNumberId, accessToken: decrypt(number.accessToken) } (decrypt may throw); else falls back to { phoneNumberId: number.phoneNumberId ?? META_PHONE_NUMBER_ID ?? null, accessToken: META_ACCESS_TOKEN ?? null }. NOTE: callers must handle a null accessToken (missing creds) and a thrown decrypt error.
- `class NumberOwnedByOtherTenantError extends Error` (name = 'NumberOwnedByOtherTenantError'). Map to HTTP 409 in route handlers.
- `upsertNumberForUser({ userId, phoneNumber, data }): Promise<WhatsAppNumber>` where data type is `Prisma.WhatsAppNumberUncheckedUpdateInput & Prisma.WhatsAppNumberUncheckedCreateInput`. Find-then-branch on unique phoneNumber: existing+other user -> throws NumberOwnedByOtherTenantError; existing+same user -> update by id with data; none -> create({ ...data, userId, phoneNumber }) with P2002 catch rethrowing NumberOwnedByOtherTenantError. Does NOT use prisma.upsert. Pass encrypted accessToken (ciphertext from crypto.encrypt) in data, never plaintext.

Schema (prisma/schema.prisma WhatsAppNumber): added nullable/defaulted fields accessToken (String? ciphertext), tokenExpiresAt (DateTime?), displayPhoneNumber (String?), verifiedName (String?), qualityRating (String?), codeVerificationStatus (String?), platformType (String?), connectionType (String @default("manual")). verificationCode retained.

DB MIGRATION GOTCHA: `npm run db:push` (prisma db push) CANNOT run against this project's live Turso DB — the datasource url is a libsql:// URL and the Prisma CLI (5.22) rejects it with P1012 ('URL must start with file:'). The repo's established pattern for live Turso DDL is a standalone @libsql/client script (see scripts/add-media-attachments.mjs). The 8 nullable/additive columns were applied to live Turso via the new idempotent scripts/add-meta-onboarding-columns.mjs (PRAGMA table_info guard, additive ALTER TABLE only, no drops) and verified idempotent on a second run. Future schema changes to Turso should follow the same script pattern, not db:push.

Verification: crypto test harness (scripts/test-crypto.mjs) passes all 3 assertions and exits 0; `npm run build` (prisma generate && next build) compiles and type-checks clean (the DYNAMIC_SERVER_USAGE logs during static generation are pre-existing and unrelated).
